LiNo CLI Tool for managing links data store

Usage: clink [OPTIONS] [QUERY]

Arguments:
  [QUERY]  LiNo query for CRUD operation

Options:
  -d, --db <DB>, --data-source <DB>, --data <DB>
          Path to the links database file [default: db.links]
  -q, --query <QUERY>, --apply <QUERY>, --do <QUERY>
          LiNo query for CRUD operation
      --indexed-lookups
          Use optional lookup-index decorators for local links and names (Rust only)
  -t, --trace
          Enable trace (verbose output), including each transport event of
          --serve, --connect and --forward (as CLINK_IPC_TRACE=1 does)
      --auto-create-missing-references
          Create missing numeric and named references as self-referential point links
  -s, --structure <STRUCTURE>
          ID of the link to format its structure
  -b, --before
          Print the state of the database before applying changes
  -c, --changes
          Print the changes applied by the query
  -a, --after, --links
          Print the state of the database after applying changes
      --in <IN>, --lino-input <IN>, --import <IN>
          Read and import a LiNo file into the database
      --in-max-depth <N>
          LiNo import nesting limit (1 to 128; default: 64)
      --out <OUT>, --lino-output <OUT>, --export <OUT>
          Write the complete database as a LiNo file
      --import-binary <PATH>, --binary-input <PATH>, --binary-in <PATH>
          Read and import a store archive in binary links notation
      --export-binary <PATH>, --binary-output <PATH>, --binary-out <PATH>
          Write the complete database, names included, as a store archive in
          binary links notation
      --always
          Store the query as an always-on persistent transformation trigger
      --once
          Store the query as a persistent transformation trigger that deletes
          itself after it fires
      --never
          Remove stored persistent transformation triggers matching the query
      --triggers
          Enable persistent transformation triggers for this command
      --triggers-file <FILE>
          Path to the persistent transformation trigger links database
          (default: <db>.triggers.links)
      --embed-triggers
          Store persistent transformation triggers directly in the main links
          database
      --transactions
          Enable the transactions layer (default log path: <db>.transitions.log)
      --transactions-file <FILE>
          Path to the transitions log store (implies --transactions)
      --commit-mode <MODE>
          Choose 'sync' or 'async' commits (default: sync, implies --transactions)
      --retention <SPEC>
          Log retention policy: 'infinite', 'sized:<n>', or 'chunked:<n>:<dir>'
          (implies --transactions)
      --vc
          Enable the version-control decorator (implies --transactions)
      --vc-file <FILE>
          Path to the version-control branches store
          (default: <db>.versioncontrol.links)
      --branch <NAME>
          Switch to a branch (creating it if --branch-from is also passed).
          Implies --vc.
      --branch-from <SEQ>
          When creating a branch with --branch, fork from this sequence point
      --checkout <POINT>
          Time-travel to a specific transition sequence or named tag.
          Implies --vc.
      --tag <NAME[=POINT]>
          Create a tag at current head or at a sequence/existing tag.
          Uses the first '=' whose complete suffix resolves.
          Implies --vc.
      --list-branches
          List version-control branches and exit
      --list-tags
          List version-control tags and exit
      --log
          Print the transitions log and exit (implies --transactions)
      --serve <ADDR>
          Serve the database on an endpoint until stopped: a TCP address
          (e.g. 127.0.0.1:7878) or KIND:ADDRESS for another transport, such as
          unix:/tmp/links.sock, pipe:NAME, fifo:DIR, shm:DIR, mmap:DIR, file:DIR,
          signal:DIR, mq:DIR, sysvmq:DIR, udp:HOST:PORT, stdio, mailslot:DIR,
          copydata:DIR or alpc:DIR (see docs/protocol/ipc-transports-v1.md);
          repeat it to serve one store on several endpoints at once. Each
          message may use the text or the binary LiNo protocol
      --forward <ADDR>
          With --serve: relay every connection, byte for byte, to this
          endpoint instead of serving a database (stacks transports)
      --graphql
          With --serve: speak Hasura's GraphQL over HTTP and WebSocket for Deep
      --jwt-secret <SECRET>
          Signs the tokens of --graphql (default: random for each run)
      --graphql-admin-secret <SECRET>
          The x-hasura-admin-secret that bypasses --permissions in --graphql
      --deep-package <FILE>
          Load a Deep package (JSON rows of links) before --graphql serves
      --connect <ADDR>
          Send the query to a clink server on a --serve endpoint (e.g.
          127.0.0.1:7878 or shm:/tmp/links) instead of opening a database;
          an empty query reads every link
      --protocol <PROTOCOL>
          'text' or 'binary' for --connect (default: text); 'text', 'binary'
          or 'any' for --serve (default: any)
      --external-references
          Binary protocol: send numbers and characters as external references
      --arity <RANGE>
          Binary protocol: link lengths to use, 'n', 'min..max' or 'min..'
          (default: 2, doublets only; e.g. 2..3 adds triplets, 1.. any length)
      --packed-widths
          Binary protocol: give each section of links the narrowest reference
          width it needs instead of one width for the whole packet
      --triplets
          With --serve: read every request as triplets, (create: (type from to)),
          (each: (index type from to)) and three-part substitutions, over this
          store of doublets; without it, every request is about doublets
      --permissions <RULES>
          Check every read and write against permission rules stored as links:
          'self' (rules in the data) or a links file of rules; without it,
          nothing is checked
      --subject <LINK>
          The subject (a link index or name) queries run as with --permissions,
          and the subject of --serve connections before (auth: token)
          (default: 0, a guest)
      --tokens <TOKENS>
          The token table of (auth: token) for --serve, --grant-token and
          --revoke-token: 'self' (tokens in the data) or a links file
      --grant-token <TOKEN>
          Let a token authenticate as --subject in the --tokens table, then exit
      --revoke-token <TOKEN>
          Forget a token of the --tokens table, then exit
      --token <TOKEN>
          With --connect: authenticate with (auth: token) before sending the query
      --lock <MODE>
          How concurrent invocations on one store are serialized: 'flock'
          (default; an OS lock on <db>.lock, released when the holder exits),
          'pid' (the directory <db>.lock.d, broken once its owner process is
          gone) or 'none'. Writers lock exclusively, read-only runs share it
      --no-lock
          Same as --lock none, for callers that serialize access themselves
      --lock-timeout <MS>
          How long to wait for a locked store before failing with the name of
          its owner (default: 30000; 0 fails at once)
      --lock-status
          Print who holds the locks of the store, then exit
  -h, --help
          Print help
  -V, --version
          Print version
